chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Safwan, from al-'Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

The freed slave (mamluk) if he has a slave-wife under him, and he divorces her, then his master frees her, she remains with him as one divorce. If not for the fact that his divorce is effective according to some of the cases we mentioned, she would be with him as two divorces, as she was initially. Because in that case, he does not possess a divorce that is valid for him to effectuate, and this also indicates that.

key_terms.التَّطْلِيقَتَيْنِ: The two divorces (referring to the count of divorces in the marriage)
key_terms.الْمَمْلُوكُ: The slave (male), specifically one who is not fully free but has some status
key_terms.مَمْلُوكَةٌ: A slave-wife (female slave owned by the husband)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a slave-wife's divorce status when her master frees her after her slave-husband divorces her?
ai.summary: In *Al-Istibsar*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to clarify the complex interplay of ownership and marital authority in a master-slave hierarchy. The Imam explains that while the slave-husband’s divorce is valid, it is considered 'defective' in terms of full independent authority because the master retains ultimate control, thus preventing the count from reaching two divorces. This highlights the Shia juristic principle that the master's right to divorce his slave-wife supersedes or modifies the slave-husband's action in this specific configuration.
